newsitem.title: CHINA: China foreign debt now $110 bln - central banker.
newsitem.headline: China foreign debt now $110 bln - central banker.

text.p: China's foreign debt currently stood at $110 billion, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday, quoting central bank governor Dai Xianglong.
Every year, China needed to fork out $30 billion to cover principal and interest payments on foreign debts and for remittances of profits by China-based foreign enterprises, Dai said.
As of June, China's total outstanding foreign debt was $109.57 billion, according to previous official figures.
Dai said China foreign exchange reserves had topped $100 billion -- one of the largest in the world. He did not elaborate.
He said China's foreign reserves were "adequate but still cannot be said to be excessive".
China's debt service ratio was 7.3 percent in 1995, well within the recognised safety level of 20 percent, newspapers have said.
